steps.title: Pick a game
steps.text: The host opens Quiz'in, then picks a game and a theme.

steps.title: Show it on the TV
steps.text: They cast the game to the TV with a Chromecast, or open the link on a computer connected to the TV.

steps.title: Guests join
steps.text: A QR code or a 4-character code is all it takes. They play in their phone browser, nothing to install.

faq.a: To show the game on the TV, yes: a Chromecast or a TV with built-in Chromecast. Otherwise, open the link on a computer connected to the TV.

faq.q: Do guests need to install the app?
faq.a: No, they scan the QR code (or type the code) and play in their phone browser.
Nothing: the app is free, with no ads and no in-app purchases.
No, neither for the host nor for the players. A first name is enough.

help.title: Help
help.sub: Trouble showing the game or joining? Here are the most common answers.

items.q: My TV doesn't show up in the list
items.a: Check that the phone and the Chromecast are on the same Wi-Fi network (not a guest network), with no VPN. On iPhone, also check that "Local Network" is turned on for Quiz'in in Settings, then restart the app.
Open the display link in the browser of a computer connected to the TV (HDMI cable) or of your smart TV, then go full screen.
Check that they scan the QR code on screen, or that they type the 4-character code correctly. An up-to-date browser is required.

items.q: How do I play in teams?
items.a: From 4 players, the teams option appears in the lobby settings.

legal.title: Legal information

privacySections.p: Quiz'in is published by [TO FILL IN: publisher name, see the legal notice]. The publisher decides how the data described here is used. Contact: quizinsupport@gmail.com.

No account is created. To play, you enter a first name (or nickname) and can pick an avatar. During a game we also record the game code, your answers, your scores, your drawings (in Draw Me) and the settings chosen by the host. An anonymous connection identifies your device while you play, with no link to your identity. We do not ask for an email, phone number, contacts, location, photos or microphone access. A nickname is enough: avoid entering your full name.
Your name, avatar, answers and drawings are visible to the other players in the game and shown on the TV. Avoid putting personal information in them.

privacySections.h: What the data is used for
privacySections.p: Only to run the game: connecting you, showing questions, counting points, showing answers and drawings. The legal basis is performance of the service (GDPR art. 6.1.b). We also rely on our legitimate interest in protecting the service from abuse (art. 6.1.f). There are no ads, no data resale and no profiling. [TO CHECK: the app uses no analytics or crash reporting tool; otherwise, say so here.]

privacySections.h: Local network and casting to the TV
privacySections.p: To find your TV, the app asks for "local network" access on iPhone. It is only used to spot Chromecast devices on your Wi-Fi: no data is collected this way. Casting to the TV goes through Google Cast, a Google service.

We use Google (Firebase: anonymous sign-in, realtime database and page hosting; Google Cast for casting). If the Blind test is turned on, music previews are provided by Deezer, which may receive your IP address during playback. Apple and Google distribute the app and apply their own rules. We do not sell any data.

Game data is stored on Google's servers (Firebase Realtime Database), in the [TO CHECK: database region, e.g. Belgium or United States] region. The site and game pages are served by Google's network (Firebase Hosting), located in several countries. We have no servers of our own. When data is processed outside the European Union, it is covered by Google's standard contractual clauses or by the EU–US Data Privacy Framework. On your phone, the app only keeps a few local settings [TO CHECK: list, e.g. remembered first name and sound]; they disappear when you uninstall the app.

Games are temporary: [TO CHECK: duration and deletion mechanism, e.g. automatic deletion 24 hours after the game ends]. The anonymous identifier is kept [TO CHECK: duration]. When you leave a game or uninstall the app, nothing more remains on your phone.
Quiz'in is made for family play. The app creates no account and shows no ads. We advise parents to accompany younger players and to choose a nickname rather than a full name.
Exchanges with the servers are encrypted (HTTPS) and access to the database is limited by security rules. No system is perfect: if something goes wrong, write to us.

You can ask for access to your data, its correction, its deletion, a restriction of its processing, or object to its processing (GDPR, art. 15 to 21). You can also withdraw a consent at any time. Write to quizinsupport@gmail.com: we reply within one month, free of charge. Since there is no account, we can only find you if you help us: give the game code, the name you used, the date and your phone type. If we cannot identify you with certainty, we cannot act on the request, so as not to hand someone else's data to the wrong person. If you think your rights are not respected, you can complain to the CNIL (cnil.fr, 3 place de Fontenoy, TSA 80715, 75334 Paris Cedex 07, France).
We may update this policy. The date of the last update is shown at the top of the page.
